statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Elevated Tail reflects a materially negative Nasdaq futures gap with aligned energy, rates and Asian-equity pressure, while direct evidence of repeated failed NQ retracements remains incomplete.
recommendation: Current machine mapping is orange because Tail is above the block threshold; subsequent classification depends on whether price discovery develops meaningful retracements or renewed directional extension.
headline: Elevated Tail persists as Nasdaq futures underperform amid oil, rates and Asian-equity pressure
body: Latest verified reporting showed Nasdaq futures about 1.1% lower versus roughly 0.5% for S&P futures, Brent above $107, and broad Asian equity weakness. The energy shock, near-5% U.S. 10-year yield and technology-specific AI caution create multiple current amplifiers, but sufficiently granular live NQ retracement evidence remains incomplete.

lookbackSummary: Tail was low at 19% through 21:00 UTC on September 13, moved to WATCH at the Globex reopening hour, and then entered the elevated band as the Nasdaq futures gap, energy shock and cross-asset pressure persisted into Asia.
outlookSummary: Near-term Tail remains elevated through the Asia-to-Europe handoff while the Nasdaq gap and energy/rates pressure remain unresolved. The forecast conditionally de-escalates with meaningful gap repair and two-way trade, but reintroduces elevated risk around the U.S. cash open if directional efficiency returns.

forecast.analysis: Latest verified reporting had Nasdaq futures about 1.1% lower and underperforming S&P futures, with Brent above $107 and Asian equities weak. Delayed Finviz context also showed NQ lagging ES. Direct evidence of repeated failed NQ retracements remains incomplete.
drivers: Nasdaq futures gap remains materially negative in latest verified reporting
Oil above $107 reinforces inflation and yield pressure
Direct NQ pullback structure is not sufficiently verified

news.title: Shares skid in Asia as oil rises, rate hikes loom
Oil prices jump more than 2% after new strikes on Saudi, Strait of Hormuz

forecast.analysis: If the Asian session keeps the Nasdaq gap largely unrepaired and rebounds remain limited, the multi-asset pressure would keep Tail elevated. A clear two-way recovery or deeper retracement would argue against further escalation.
drivers: Conditional gap persistence through early Asia
Oil and rate pressure remain potential directional amplifiers
Meaningful retracement would reduce Tail evidence

forecast.analysis: Risk remains elevated if Asian trading continues to preserve the technology-led futures discount. Tail can ease if NQ develops sustained two-way trade rather than extending from failed rebounds.
drivers: Asia-session gap repair is the primary checkpoint
Nasdaq underperformance versus broader futures remains relevant
Two-way price discovery would weaken the one-way-path thesis

forecast.analysis: Ahead of the Europe handoff, elevated Tail is conditional on the gap staying open and cross-asset stress remaining aligned. A retracement that holds would weaken the case for persistent mean-reversion failure.
drivers: Conditional persistence of the Nasdaq discount

news.title: Oil prices jump more than 2% after new strikes on Saudi, Strait of Hormuz

forecast.analysis: The European cash-open transition can amplify an existing gap if equities, yields and oil align in the same direction. Tail stays elevated only if NQ also fails to produce meaningful retracements during that transition.
drivers: Cross-asset alignment can reinforce the opening gap
Failed NQ retracements would be required for stronger Tail evidence

forecast.analysis: After the European open, Tail remains elevated if the Nasdaq discount persists without meaningful recovery. Stabilizing oil, yields or technology futures would reduce directional efficiency even if headline stress stays extreme.
drivers: Oil stabilization would reduce one amplifier

forecast.analysis: Tail sits at the lower edge of the elevated band if Europe does not repair the gap. A sequence of deeper rebounds would support de-escalation toward WATCH; renewed extension from shallow pullbacks would keep the orange mapping.
drivers: Gap-repair quality after the Europe transition

forecast.analysis: WATCH becomes plausible if the overnight gap begins to repair and cross-asset pressure stops reinforcing the same direction. Persistence near session extremes or another failed rebound would invalidate that easing path.

A two-way European morning would keep Tail in WATCH despite very high event stress. The key distinction remains whether volatility is being mean-reverted or converted into repeated directional extension.
drivers: Geopolitical energy risk remains a stress driver

forecast.analysis: U.S. premarket participation raises event sensitivity. Tail remains WATCH unless the premarket shows renewed one-way extension, shallow pullbacks and broad confirmation from yields, volatility and technology leadership.

The U.S. cash-open hour is a high-sensitivity checkpoint. Tail would be elevated if the overnight gap survives the opening auction and rebounds fail; a decisive retracement through the opening range would argue for a lower score.

The first full cash-session hour carries the highest conditional Tail in this forecast. Repeated extension after failed pullbacks would validate the elevated score; durable two-way trade would quickly weaken it.
drivers: Repeated extension after failed pullbacks is the key Tail condition
Two-way trade is the main de-escalation condition

forecast.analysis: If the opening impulse remains efficient into mid-morning, Tail stays elevated. If breadth and large technology names diverge from the index move or pullbacks deepen, the path would become less hostile to mean reversion.
drivers: Breadth conflict would reduce directional conviction

forecast.analysis: Late U.S. morning risk remains elevated only if the market continues to reject meaningful retracements. A settled range with repeated reversals would shift the regime toward mixed conditions despite high macro stress.

WATCH is favored if the U.S. session has transitioned into two-way trade by midday. A fresh catalyst-driven break that holds near an extreme would be the main reason for Tail to remain above the block threshold.
drivers: Fresh persistent break is the main upside Tail risk

forecast.analysis: Midday conditions are forecast to be less directionally efficient if earlier gaps have been partially repaired. Tail would re-escalate only if a new information wave restores one-way structure.
drivers: Conditional gap repair by U.S. midday
New information wave could re-escalate Tail

forecast.analysis: The U.S. power-hour approach can revive directional risk. Tail remains WATCH unless a late-session move is confirmed by shallow pullbacks, technology leadership and cross-asset alignment.

After the main cash session, Tail can ease if the close does not preserve one-way structure. A large closing imbalance or unresolved geopolitical shock would keep the overnight transition more fragile.

Early evening Tail stays in WATCH while markets digest the U.S. close and the energy shock. The score assumes no new discontinuity; a fresh supply or security escalation would invalidate the easing path.

WATCH persists if volatility remains elevated but price discovery is two-sided. Tail would rise again only if the next overnight session inherits a clear directional imbalance with weak retracement behavior.

The baseline shifts to low Tail if the prior session has absorbed the gap and no persistent second leg has emerged. Stress can remain extreme even while the pathological no-retracement path becomes less probable.
drivers: Conditional absorption of the prior gap
High stress does not by itself imply high Tail

forecast.analysis: Low Tail remains conditional on continued two-way trade and the absence of a new geopolitical or rates discontinuity. Scheduled events later in the week remain checkpoints rather than observed future outcomes.

The overnight baseline remains low Tail if markets continue to mean-revert and cross-asset volatility does not re-align directionally. Any renewed session-extreme holding would invalidate this baseline.
drivers: Cross-asset alignment remains an invalidation risk

forecast.analysis: The final forecast hour keeps low Tail under an orderly overnight baseline. This does not assume calm markets; it assumes volatility remains sufficiently two-sided to avoid a persistent mean-reversion failure path.
drivers: Persistent one-way structure is not assumed
Volatility may remain high without a Tail regime shift

forecastDetail.comment: Current evidence supports elevated Tail from the unrepaired Nasdaq discount and aligned oil/rates/Asia pressure, but repeated failed NQ retracements are not yet sufficiently verified.
Tail remains elevated conditionally if the Asian gap persists; meaningful two-way recovery would weaken the one-way-path evidence.
The main checkpoint is whether Asia repairs the technology-led futures discount or preserves it through shallow rebounds.
Europe pre-open keeps Tail elevated only if the gap and cross-asset pressure remain aligned; a durable retracement would support easing.
The European open can amplify the overnight move, but stronger Tail requires NQ itself to reject meaningful retracements.
Post-open European trade remains an evidence checkpoint: persistent Nasdaq weakness supports elevation, while stabilization weakens it.
